claims.temporal_assessment: No pre-OSS affiliation or employer is accepted from the conflicting Army row.
claims.match_notes: Keep the conflict visible and inspect Box 553 and the original source card.

claims.claim_text: Lester C Neimann's protected identifier conflicts with surname spellings in the official Army bulk file and another OSS index entity.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier reaches Army surname NIEMANN and is shared by a separate OSS index entity spelled NIEMAN; the present row reads NEIMANN.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting; a shared identifier and materially different surname spellings cannot justify an automatic merge.
claims.temporal_assessment: No employment or pre-OSS affiliation is accepted from the conflicting Army row.
claims.match_notes: Keep the entities separate until direct personnel-file evidence resolves the duplicate cluster.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Julian M Neimczylc is probably Julian Martin Niemczyk.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare first-and-middle-name combination and close surname spelling align with a detailed Army-to-OSS oral history and an official CIA-hosted OSS veterans roster.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable; the match is distinctive and context-rich but lacks a protected identifier or direct personnel-file link.
claims.temporal_assessment: The oral history explicitly sequences university attendance, Army service, and transfer to OSS.
claims.match_notes: Preserve Neimczylc as the indexed spelling and Niemczyk as a qualified documented variant.
